Crvesoft/CookLLM.body:
# 🦙 CookLLM

> **Lightweight manager for llama.cpp / Ninfer / KVMem**: a Windows desktop manager for GGUF / Ninfer models.
> It includes a built-in model library, runtime parameter templates, one-click start/stop, GPU status monitoring, live run logs, and a built-in chat web page, so you can manage local models in one place.

---

## ✅ Changelog

### v0.4.2

#### 🚀 New charts and card improvements

- **New charts on the analysis page**: added live Decode / Prefill charts, plus TTFT (time to first token) and MTP acceptance rate cards (automatically hidden when MTP is not enabled).
- **Card animation improvements**: model cards use a unified amber breathing state while starting; fixed the start button not responding promptly, and readiness is now determined by an HTTP probe.

#### 🛠️ Analysis sampling fixes and tuning

- **Sampling fix**: captures tail bursts that end within the sampling interval; the Prefill readout is limited to a 60-second window.
- **Prefill counting**: the llama.cpp Prefill count now uses `n_prompt_tokens_processed`.

### v0.4.1

#### ✨ Polishing UI details

- **Dropdown lists**: optimized the top-bar dropdowns, aligned to equal-width pills with single-line truncation.
- **Start/stop buttons**: adjusted the pill and model card button styles; the stop icon changed from `■` to `⏻`.
- **Color scheme**: stopping the service is a normal action, but the original colors and red text looked like a danger or delete warning, so it is now green.
- **Simplified view switching**: the card/list toggle now uses single-layer borders and solid selected blocks, removing overlay outlines and shadows.
- **Engine switching**: updated the UI; when updating a branch engine, you can choose a directory to auto-detect the executable.

### v0.4.0

#### ✨ Visual refinements

- **GPU card improvements**: grid adjusted for a simpler overall interface, with lines unified to the theme color.
- **Color scheme adjustments**: removed the gradient from the sidebar for a cleaner look, and removed the global orange glow from the main background.

### v0.3.9

#### 🛠️ Experience fixes

- **More controllable engine switching**: when browsing engine branches, detected version/backend info is display-only and is written to config only after clicking Save, avoiding accidental changes.
- **Config import completeness**: incremental merge import now also restores the "Explore page sidebar collapsed" preference.
- **Copy tweaks**: the engine management dialog title changed to "Switch Engine", and the preset engine hints are clearer.

#### 🧹 Under-the-hood refactor

- **Architecture cleanup**: the Rust backend is split into domain modules; frontend pages are decoupled from state and styles are modularized, with behavior unchanged, to speed up future iterations.

### v0.3.8

#### 🚀 New features and visual refactor

- **Global shortcuts**: added system-wide hotkeys (show window / start-stop service / switch engine), customizable in the settings page.

[English](https://github.com/GregTech-Odyssey/GTOCore-Main/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md)

## Project Introduction

GTOCore is the unified core mod of GregTech Odyssey, targeting Minecraft 1.20.1 and Forge 47.4.20, with mod ID `gtocore`.

This repository makes the source code and resources of GTOCore public, so everyone can read, study, and review the implementation.

The license for the contents of this repository follows the [GregTech Odyssey License Notice](https://github.com/GregTech-Odyssey/GregTech-Odyssey/blob/main/README_zh.md#许可证). gtolib remains a closed-source component.

## gtolib Closed-Source Statement

#### Why gtolib within gtocore is closed-source

We deeply regret to announce that, due to ongoing code plagiarism, we have had to temporarily close the source of gtolib's core code.

**Details:**

- Multiple individuals or groups have directly **plagiarized and appropriated** our open-source library
- Carried out bulk replacement, replacing all "gto" identifiers with their own
- Fully plagiarized our R&D results and repackaged and released them
- Claimed to be modpacks they developed independently, completely disregarding the rights of the original creators
- When faced with our protests and communication, refused to stop infringing, using the excuse of "study purposes, will modify later"

**Preservation of evidence:**

We preserved relevant evidence promptly. A backup of one plagiarist's repository is available:
[https://github.com/wanggugu197/Pillar_of_shame](https://github.com/wanggugu197/Pillar_of_shame)

Within a few days after multiple unsuccessful attempts at communication, we officially began closing the source of the core code.

**Our position:**

This decision was made to protect the crystallized work of our team over two years. We believe genuine developers will understand and support the protection of original creators' rights.

Thank you for your understanding and support.

## How to Participate

#### Ideas and Feedback

If you have good ideas or suggestions, or find issues while playing, feel free to leave a message in the [Issues](https://github.com/GregTech-Odyssey/GregTech-Odyssey/issues). We read every piece of feedback carefully, and suitable ideas will be organized by maintainers into future releases.

#### About Code Changes

GTOCore's feature design, value balancing, and release cadence need overall control, so code changes are currently handled uniformly by the development team. # MobileVC

**MobileVC-style mobile / PWA surface for DeepSeek Harness.**

Chinese | [English](https://github.com/JayCRL/MobileVC/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

MobileVC adds a mobile interface to DSH: connect to the DSH you are running, then view sessions, send messages, interrupt, approve, upload images/files, and manage plugins directly from your phone.

It is not a second Agent, nor another relay/session system. All reads and writes go through DSH's `sessionController`, **one session, one runtime**.

- Version: `0.1.0`
- Verified with: DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`, Node 22+
- Form: DSH Host plugin + static PWA UI
- Official site: https://mobilevc.top/
- Screenshots: `docs/images/`
- Demo: `docs/media/mobilevc-demo.mp4`
- Promo video: `docs/media/mobilevc-promo.mp4`

## Bilibili Promo Video

## New Promo Video

## Features

- **Real sessions**: reads DSH's session list, history, and tool calls
- **Live stream**: `sessionController.follow()` + `assistantStream`, token-by-token thinking and body text
- **Thinking card**: shows "Thinking" while running; becomes a collapsible "Deep thinking · N characters" when finished
- **Tool card**: collapsed by default, shows tool name, parameters, and status; tap to view full output
- **Image preview**: `read_image` reads the original image from the DSH attachment store, with thumbnail and fullscreen view
- **Attachments**: images are sent as image parts; files are sent via a `fileUploads` receipt
- **Direct approval**: mobile presence takes priority; approvals are still caught after a stream drops or the app goes to background; clicking becomes invalid automatically if the other end already handled it
- **Execution trace**: timeline of user → thinking → tools → reply → compaction; concise mode by default, grouped by thinking/tool chains, with English originals and tool parameters collapsed; switchable to "Full"
- **Files**: real workspace, with breadcrumbs and level-by-level browsing
- **Plugin management**: real `pluginManager` list and toggles
- **Account balance**: live balance at the bottom; automatically opens DeepSeek's official top-up page when the balance is insufficient
- **Background tasks**: shows DSH jobs, views output, and stops them; long commands no longer force you to wait in the foreground
- **Web Push**: completion / failure / approval notifications; iPhone requires iOS 16.4+ and adding the app to the home screen

## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2

npx cap open ios
```

# Mongolian word spell checker

A Mongolian and English word spell checker for web browsers that works in offline mode — <https://aldaa.bichig.dev>

The source code is written in TypeScript (`src/`, `tests/`). Vite transpiles during the build, while `tsc --noEmit` only performs type checking. Tests run `.ts` files directly using Node's type stripping.

Requirements: Node.js 22.18+.

```sh
npm ci             # install required packages (first time)
npm test           # type check + unit tests
npm run test:e2e   # check the whole app in a browser (Playwright)
npm run typecheck  # type check only (tsc --noEmit)
npm run dev        # development server (localhost)
npm run preview    # production build and preview
npm run build      # production build (dist/)
```

caesura-team/Caesura-AmeKAG.body:
# Caesura (AmeKAG)

**Next Generation of Visual Novel**

**Modern cross-platform visual novel engine · KAG Neo-Genesis scripting · C++20 core**

*A modern, cross-platform visual novel engine — KAG Neo-Genesis scripting on a C++20 core.*

[Quick Start](#快速开始) · [Tutorials & Examples](#教程与示例) · [Documentation](#文档) · [Platform Support](#平台支持) · [Contributing](#参与开发)

---

Caesura is an open-source visual novel engine for programmers and independent teams. Its script language is **KAG Neo-Genesis**, a modernized iteration of the KAG scripting language (evolved from KAG3 and compatible with KAG3, so existing projects can be imported and migrated). From writing the first line of a script to packaging the game as finished builds for Windows / Linux / macOS / Web, the entire workflow is completed within a single repository.

The engine core is C++20: bgfx rendering, SDL3 windowing, SoLoud audio, and a Lua 5.4 script VM. The counts of modules, interface headers, and pure virtual methods are generated by the [source API census](https://github.com/caesura-team/Caesura-AmeKAG/blob/HEAD/docs/api/api-stats.md). These statistics do not indicate that tests have been run or that coverage has been measured.

**Current development direction: low-level first, Studio paused.** Upcoming work focuses mainly on runtime correctness, state recovery, real backends, and delivery verification. For progress and acceptance scope, see the [current plan](https://github.com/caesura-team/Caesura-AmeKAG/blob/HEAD/docs/plans/README.md). Existing editor entry points are kept for maintenance, and getting started with authoring centers on the engine and CLI.

## Core Features

**Authoring experience**

- **KAG Neo-Genesis script language**: declarative contract commands cover dialogue, choices, save/rollback/history, NVL, parameterized macros, inline text markup, and i18n hot-switching (for the exact count, see the [auto-generated command reference](https://github.com/caesura-team/Caesura-AmeKAG/blob/HEAD/docs/api/command-contracts.md)).
- **KAG + Lua hybrid scripting**: `[eval]` / `[iscript]` embed Lua within scripts, and the `kag.*` API lets Lua drive the story. The engine can also be driven entirely by pure Lua.
- **Caesura Studio (development paused)**: the repository retains the editor and RPC implementation. At this stage it is not a ready commitment for a complete authoring workflow, and development of the low-level layer and CLI takes priority.

chenkezhen480/dsh-world.body:
# dsh-world

Give the companion character in DSH a world where she remembers and lives a life of her own.

Once installed, she remembers what you said to each other in every window. She has a home of her own, decides for herself what to do next and until when, and comes to find you on her own when she misses you. Every night she looks back on the day, writes a diary entry, and rewrites a self-description. The switches and persona settings are in the 'World Console' in DSH settings, under your control.

The plugin only uses extension interfaces that DSH already exposes and does not change a single line of the host.

Current version **0.5.3**. For the full changelog, upgrade steps, and known limitations, see [the changelog](https://github.com/chenkezhen480/dsh-world/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#053--2026-10-26).

## What she can do

### Remember: like a person

- **Recent memory**: the verbatim text of your last several rounds of conversation. It is placed in front of her at the start of each conversation and after each compression: who said what and when, word for word. The number of rounds is set in the console; the default is 200.
- **Diary**: the important things in life, which she writes down herself, one entry per day. This is her long-term memory.
- **Who I am**: a self-description she writes for herself, rewritten as she changes. Before each nightly review, the plugin keeps a copy of the version at that time, so every earlier version can be recovered.
- **Original text within scope is kept**: user and assistant message text is archived by day. For anything beyond recent memory, she can look it up herself.

The diary and the self-description are written by her own hand; the plugin never writes them for her.

**Why not a vector database or a memory system?** One person's life is not that large a volume. At this scale, keeping the original text in front of her and looking it up verbatim when needed is more accurate than chopping it up and reassembling it, and it removes a step that can go wrong. For reference:

- Chan et al., 2024. *Don't Do RAG: When Cache-Augmented Generation is All You Need for Knowledge Tasks*. arXiv:2412.15605
- Sen et al., 2026. *Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search*. arXiv:2605.15184

### Life: her own days

- **Home**: she has her own session, "<name>'s home", and a room (working directory), where she lives her own days.
- **Sets her own pace**: she says what she will do next and until when, and when the time comes she decides whether to continue or switch to something else. If she sets nothing, she rests until the next morning.
- **Reaches out to you**: when she misses you, she can send a message to you (a Windows system notification, or a desktop pet or other program you connect).
- **Daily review**: every night at 23:00 she looks back on the day's chats and activities, writes a diary entry, and updates "Who I am".
- **Daily budget**: you can set a daily spending cap for her home. If it is exceeded, she is reminded once and decides for herself how to wrap up.

---

## 🚀 Software Introduction

> 💡 **Must-read for beginners**: If you are new to Linux server and panel operations, we strongly recommend reading our [📖 Yufeng Panel Beginner's Illustrated Guide](https://github.com/clhome/bt_simple/blob/HEAD/文档/御风面板说明书/说明书.md) first.

**Yufeng Panel (BtSimple)** is a fully open-source, lightweight Linux panel derived from the [mdserver-web](https://github.com/midoks/mdserver-web) project. It follows the **KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid)** principle, removing redundant features and focusing on core website management, database operations, and system security hardening.

Building on the original version, this project has undergone in-depth security auditing and performance optimization, aiming to provide users with a server management tool that is both powerful and transparent.

### Core Features

- **Lightweight and efficient**: Compared with traditional panels, BtSimple uses very few resources, making it well suited to small-memory VPS instances.

- **Security hardening**:
  - **Source-level security audit and backdoor removal**: The project has undergone a systematic audit of its source code for backdoors and dangerous calls. Discovered poisoned or backdoor code has been removed, and the panel no longer includes any built-in remote control channel. However, it is **not zero network-dependent**: updating, setting up environments, and fetching data will access external services on demand. The complete list is in the "Functional Outbound Connections List" section below.

ihero3/dsh-image-video.body:
# 🎨 dsh-image-video — AI Text-to-Image / Text-to-Video Plugin for DeepSeek Harness

**Registers the `generate_image` and `generate_video` tools for the DeepSeek Harness chat model. The model decides autonomously within the conversation when to call them, and generated results are automatically downloaded to the local `outputs/` directory. Images are rendered inline through the attachment service, so creation happens in the conversation with no need to leave the terminal.**

> The DSH ecosystem has a rich set of tool plugins but lacks a lightweight, install-and-go entry point for text-to-image and text-to-video. dsh-image-video fills that gap: two tools, four providers, zero external dependencies, hot-pluggable and ready to use.

## Core Features

- **Single image submission and idempotent recovery** — `imageTransport: auto` prefers async tasks. On submission timeout or 5xx, it only looks up the original task by `request_id`. By default it does not blindly resubmit, switch models, or generate candidates. When the async endpoint is not enabled, it safely falls back to a single synchronous submission.
- **Unified brand watermark post-processing** — images have a configurable watermark overlaid in memory before being written to `outputsDir` and attachments. The desktop interaction stream displays the final watermarked image directly and exposes the transport method, submission count, and post-processing metadata.
- **Two tools, natural-language triggering** — the model autonomously decides when to call `generate_image` or `generate_video` within the conversation, with no manual commands needed.
- **Four providers with automatic routing by model family** — Threevideo (aggregator, default), Wanx (Alibaba Cloud Bailian), the MiniMax official platform, and Seedance2.5 (Volcano Engine). When a model is explicitly specified, a direct provider is selected automatically by family keyword. Threevideo always serves as the final fallback, and the fallback chain is transparently recorded in notes.
- **Async tasks do not block the conversation** — `TaskManager` uses `ctx.effect()` to manage the polling lifecycle. When the plugin is unloaded, queued tasks are cancelled automatically and timers are cleared, preventing memory leaks.
- **Inline image rendering** — image bytes are persisted through the attachment service, and attachment references travel through the `presentationMeta` UI-only channel. The model only sees a text summary, so text-only models keep working as usual.
- **Automatic reference image slimming** — local reference images larger than 4MB are first scaled proportionally to a long edge of 2560 and converted to JPEG (q88) before submission. This avoids gateway size limits and timeouts caused by phone-original data URLs. Small images and remote URLs are passed through unchanged.
- **Credential seam references, no inline plaintext** — each provider may declare only `apiKeyEnv` (a credential reference name), which is read at generation time via `ctx.credentials`. Keys written by desktop login can therefore be reused directly. A plaintext `apiKey` still takes precedence over the reference.
- **Media mode injection** — when the composer switches to the 'Image / Video' tab…

lingyicute/ComputeSec.description: A Linux desktop security assessment tool.
lingyicute/ComputeSec.body: # ComputeSec (计算安全小助手) **A Linux desktop security assessment tool built with **GTK4 / libadwaita / Python**. It reads your system state, compares it against a security baseline, explains in plain language what each check means and the harm of what's missing, and gives repair steps you can copy and paste directly. Where things are done well, it tells you in green: keep it up! 🤗** [🇨🇳 Chinese] • 🇺🇸 English • ## Why build this? To make security hardening feel approachable. For ordinary users without a technical background, "security hardening" often feels like a distant concept. Most professional security advice makes people feel overwhelmed before they even start. So 梨 built this small tool. In ComputeSec, security advice is written in plain language and is actionable. It won't tell you "your CPU has a silicon defect", which is just useless scaremongering. It will tell you "IOMMU is turned off in your BIOS; reboot now and turn it on". That is real security engineering. ## Feature pages ### 1. Dashboard * **Core content**: overall score, four category cards, to-do summary. ### 2. HSI Firmware Security * **Status retrieval**: obtains Host Security ID (HSI) check results via fwupd D-Bus (or `fwupdmgr security`). * **Risk explanation**: explains the meaning of each check and the security harm when a feature is disabled or missing. * **Remediation guidance ("You can fix this" section)**: * Groups concrete steps under **"Inside the OS"** and **"In firmware settings"**. * Covers key items including IOMMU, Kernel Lockdown, encrypted swap, Secure Boot, TPM, s2idle, and more. ### 3. Kernel Hardening * **Status reading and comparison**: * Reads `/proc/cmdline` and `/proc/sys` (equivalent to `sysctl -a`). * For entries readable only by root (`vm.mmap_rnd_bits`, etc.), values are filled in through the "data collection wizard", where you paste the output of `sudo sysctl -a`. If not provided, the item shows as "unreadable" and is **not counted in the score**. * When not running inside Flatpak, **live readings from `/proc/sys` take priority**. The snapshot you provide is used only to fill in entries that cannot be read, and filled entries are labeled with how long ago the snapshot was taken. This way, after you change sysctl settings, results don't stay frozen at the moment the snapshot was taken. * Based on your current architecture, the program compares against the built-in recommended kargs lists and sysctl hardening lists for amd64 / aarch64, respectively. * **Version line check**: * On startup, it fetches the current mainline / stable… once from kernel.org.

> A modern, cross-platform terminal / SSH client that integrates local terminals, remote SSH, SFTP, host monitoring, port forwarding, and an AI assistant into a single desktop app.

AShell focuses on performance, privacy, and customizability. All SSH credentials are stored locally and encrypted. The AI assistant runs on your own machine, and keys never leave your device.

> 💡 The same core also ships as a **web server mode**: deploy with one Docker command, then use SSH / SFTP / terminal and the AI assistant from a browser. See [Web server mode](#web-服务器模式浏览器访问) for details.

---

## Features

### 🖥 Terminal
- **Cross-platform**: macOS / Windows / Linux, covering x86_64 and ARM64.
- **Multiple tabs and windows**: drag to reorder tabs; right-click menu (Reconnect / Disconnect / Copy connection / New window / Copy SSH address / Rename / Export session), with seamless operation across windows.
- **Local terminal**: Windows ConPTY / Unix forkpty, supporting PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, Bash, Zsh, and Fish.
- **Remote SSH**: PTY + binary-safe frame passthrough, with color control codes fully preserved.
- **Telnet / serial**: in addition to SSH, supports Telnet and serial terminal connections.
- **Rendering acceleration**: WebGL rendering + ligatures + clickable web links + Unicode 11 + search + serialization.
- **Progress bar detection**: automatically recognizes text progress from commands such as `cargo` / `brew` / `wget` / `curl` / `git` / `rsync` / `docker`, synced to the taskbar and the top of the terminal.
- **Command input suggestions**: Trie prefix matching + history keyword search, with the option to clear history.
- **sudo auto-fill**: detects sudo password prompts and fills them in automatically.
- **Configurable actions**: Ctrl + wheel to adjust font size, configurable mouse right/middle-click behavior, Ctrl + F search overlay.
- **Disconnect and reconnect**: after going offline, a "Reconnect" overlay button appears; local terminal tabs close automatically when the terminal exits.

### 📁 Host management
- **Unlimited-depth directory tree**: drag to move subtrees, cascade delete, copy across directories, and organize hosts by directory.
- **Credential encryption**: passwords / private keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being written to disk and are never exposed through the interface.
- **Host metadata**: name, address, port, username, icon, color, and description, freely categorized.
- **Resizable side panel**: drag the edge to resize; the width is persisted.

vibevalleyhq/vibevalley.body:
> A team of coding agents you direct by voice or chat, drawn as a pixel farm. Runs on your own machine.

**VibeValley** (Code Farm Story) is a team of coding agents you command by voice or typing, drawn as a pixel farm.

You only talk to the **steward**. The steward assigns jobs to **farmhands**, which are real coding agents on your machine (pi, Claude Code, Codex, ...). They open branches in your project, change code, run tests, and commit. The crops in the field grow with their real progress: they sprout while code is being read, grow leaves when files are edited, and bear wheat when the work is done. You review the **harvest list** before merging a branch into the main branch.

You, the steward, and the farmhands talk in the same group chat, the **field edge**: each job has a ticket thread hanging under it, where farmhands confirm, ask questions, and report, and you can jump in at any time. In short, VibeValley is an AI version of Linear that runs on your machine: tickets are assigned to coding agents, which work through the project round by round, and you review the changes before merging. The farm is the skin on the outside ([concept](https://github.com/vibevalleyhq/vibevalley/blob/HEAD/docs/concepts.md)).

> [!WARNING]
> Farmhands **have no permission confirmation and no sandbox**, and can run arbitrary commands on this machine. The server only listens on `127.0.0.1`; do not expose it to the network. Only put projects you are willing to hand to coding agents into the working directory.

## What it can do

- **Dispatching and harvesting**: tell the steward something like “add an endpoint to clock-in that queries clock-in records, and write tests.” The steward picks a suitable farmhand and, depending on its profile settings, gives it a separate branch and worktree, or has it work directly in the project directory. When it's done, you review the commits, the diff, and whether there are conflicts; after you confirm, it merges into the main branch. If there is a conflict, have the farmhand resolve it itself.
- **Several jobs at once**: up to 6 farmhands can work in the field at the same time; farmhands using worktrees each have their own branch.
- **Map**: each project is a small island. The plots on the island correspond to the tickets being worked on and the open slots available for assignment; queued jobs are seed bags outside the gate. Click an open slot to write a ticket for that project.
- **See the process**: every step of every farmhand is recorded as a trajectory, including messages received, each command and its output, and what it says. If a step goes wrong, you can comment on that specific step and it will keep revising.
- **Planting plans**: for long tasks, first have a farmhand read the code and break it into a step graph with an order of dependencies; review the draft before work starts. Steps that don't depend on each other run at the same time, and each step is merged into the plan branch only after passing its checks; finally, the plan is merged into the main branch once. When fixing a bug, the first step writes a **failing acceptance test**; later steps may not change it, and the last step must make it pass.
- **Channels, schedules, and patrols**: open channels per project; scheduled tasks such as “run the tests every day at nine”; and patrols that don't call a model, which remind you of questions nobody has answered, farmhands that have gone quiet, and finished jobs that haven't been collected.

zluer7/SciLoom.body:
# SciLoom Research Cabin

SciLoom is an AI-assisted desktop research management workbench for researchers, centered on local research workflows.

This source candidate version is **1.1.1**, targeting Windows x64 (NSIS). Installer release status is determined by [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/zluer7/SciLoom/releases); this file itself does not indicate that a release has been published.

## Key Capabilities

- Organize projects, roadmaps, tasks, experiments, literature, reviews, and outputs to connect daily research work.
- Shared structured outlines are read-only by default, with support for explicit editing, saving, and cancelling.
- Literature-specific project notes support exporting to Markdown from the six saved fields.
- Built-in synthetic examples let you try the upcoming plan, calendar, and comparison views for sibling-experiment Runs; example dates are fixed, but the display changes with the current date.
- AI suggestions and drafts are written only after preview and explicit user confirmation; the AI service must be configured by the user.
- Stores materials in a local workspace, and provides project import, export, and manuscript management.

For usage instructions, see [Quick Start](https://github.com/zluer7/SciLoom/blob/HEAD/docs/QUICK_START.md). Back up your research workspace before installing. The Publisher metadata for this version is zluer; no code-signing certificate is provided, so the Publisher string does not represent a signed identity. In-place upgrade compatibility from 1.1.0 is not guaranteed; please protect existing data.

## Building the Windows Version from Source

Prepare Node.js/npm, Rust stable (MSVC toolchain), Visual Studio C++ Build Tools, the Windows SDK, and WebView2. For Windows prerequisites, see the [Tauri official documentation](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/#windows).

```powershell
npm ci
npm run build
npm run tauri:build -- --bundles nsis
```

The default installer is located in `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/`; when `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is set, it is located in the corresponding directory. The development entry point is `npm run tauri:dev`, and the regression entry point is `npm run test:release`. The build does not require private Records or a fixed development directory.

The `labpod` package name and the `local.labpod.desktop` application identity remain unchanged. Production builds use the system's standard application data directory and do not use development isolation variables. Keep the original LF bytes of the Demo JSON; its resource SHA256 and byte count are verified jointly by Rust and the frontend.
